title: Queue Number of Planar Graphs
statement_text: A challenging open problem in the area of queue layouts is to decide whether planar graphs have constant queue number.
context_text: A queue layout of a graph is an ordering of its vertices (the spine) together with a colouring of its edges such that no two edges of the same colour are nested, where two edges are nested if their four endpoints are distinct and the endpoints of one edge induce an interval of the spine containing the endpoints of the other edge. The queue number of a graph is the minimum number of colours in a queue layout; the question is whether there is a constant $c$ such that every planar graph has queue number at most $c$. This is a known open problem from the queue-layout literature, mentioned by the authors as background. Every graph has a subdivision with queue number $2$, and Dujmović and Wood showed that graphs of bounded queue number form a class of bounded expansion (a notion of sparsity of Nešetřil and Ossona de Mendez). The paper's main theorem says that posets of bounded height whose cover graphs belong to a fixed class of bounded expansion have bounded dimension; hence posets whose cover graph has bounded queue number have dimension bounded by a function of the queue number and the height. Status note (November 2026): solved; Dujmović, Joret, Micek, Morin, Ueckerdt and Wood proved that planar graphs have bounded queue number ('Planar graphs have bounded queue-number', arXiv 2019, J. ACM 2020).
